What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Age: 24
Gender: Female
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with acute pulmonary edema due to severe aortic valve insufficiency. She had previously been diagnosed with Takayasu's disease and had undergone multiple surgeries, including replacement of the distal ascending aorta and hemiarch, stenosis of celiac artery and superior mesenteric artery, and stenosis of the orifices of both renal arteries. She had a graft used to direct blood flow from the right internal iliac artery to all stenosed arteries. She also underwent a right nephrectomy due to acute thrombosis of the right renal artery graft. The patient was on steroid treatment since the diagnosis of her disease.

Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The procedure was performed through a median sternotomy, and a composite graft with a mechanical valve was implanted. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged from the hospital on the 10th postoperative day.

Follow-up:
The patient had a one year clinical follow-up that showed normal echocardiographical results, and she was doing well in normal daily activities.

Pathology:
Part of the dilated aortic root wall was sent for histological examination, which verified the diagnosis of Takayasu's arteritis.

Note:
The patient's condition was complex and required surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she had a good one year clinical follow-up.

text:
# Principal diagnosis: M31.4 Aortic arch syndrome [Takayasu]

## Why M31.4

- The admission was for **severe aortic valve insufficiency**, treated with aortic root and valve replacement (composite graft with a mechanical valve, i.e., a Bentall-type procedure).
- The regurgitation came from a **dilated aortic root caused by Takayasu's arteritis**, which histology of the resected root wall confirmed.
- Because the valve disease is a manifestation of a systemic disease, the **dagger–asterisk convention** applies. In ICD-10-AM, the etiology (dagger) code is sequenced first:
  - **M31.4†** Aortic arch syndrome [Takayasu] (principal)
  - **I39.1\*** Aortic valve disorders in diseases classified elsewhere (manifestation, must follow)

## Likely additional diagnoses

| Code | Condition |
|---|---|
| I39.1* | Aortic insufficiency due to Takayasu's arteritis |
| I50.1 | Left ventricular failure (acute pulmonary oedema of cardiac origin) |
| I77.81 (or the applicable aortic ectasia/dilatation code in your edition) | Dilated aortic root |
| Z90.5 | Acquired absence of kidney (prior right nephrectomy) |
| Z95.88 / Z95.8 | Presence of prior vascular grafts |
| Z92.24 or Z79.x (edition-dependent) | Long-term steroid use |

## Caveat

If your coding guidance requires the clinician to explicitly document the causal link between the regurgitation and Takayasu's arteritis, query the clinician. Without that link, the valve disease would be coded as **I35.1 Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) insufficiency**, and that code would become principal, with M31.4 as an additional diagnosis.
